name: OpenClaw Agent Harness
description: Multi-agent development harness: crystallise -> plan -> execute (Sonnet) -> adversarial review (Fable-5) -> PR.

listener_enabled.description: DEPRECATED as of beta.34: IGNORED. The Slack listener was removed; the harness is tool-driven only (drive it via harness_run / harness_start_session / harness_merge_pr). A `true` value is logged and does nothing. This key is retained only for config back-compat.

channel.description: Slack channel ID (e.g. C0DEVCHAN). Only required when listener_enabled is true.

authorised_users.description: Slack user IDs allowed to open sessions or drop control reactions

credential_service.description: Vault service name for the Slack bot token. Enables reactions poller.

native_progress_delivery.description: beta.77: harness direct-posts progress/terminal headlines to Slack via the vault bot token when credential_service is set and a session has a real Slack binding (channel + non-synthetic thread). Independent of the wedge-prone agent api.sendMessage turn. Set false to force poll-only. Does not affect clarifications/inbound.

daily_max_usd.description: Hard daily spend ceiling (USD); basis for the deploy-repair budget. Must be >= daily_warn_usd.

allowed.description: Repos the harness can touch. Supports owner/repo or owner/* glob.

never_commit_paths.description: beta.114: pathspecs whose changes are reverted instead of committed -- generated trees that belong to the repo's tooling, not to any feature (e.g. ["okf/**"]). Empty by default.

worker_mechanical.description: beta.91 (Fix 3): optional cheaper/faster model for mechanical scaffolding sub-tasks (prisma models, migration, sidebar entry, barrel exports). When set, mechanical sub-tasks dispatch on this model; lead + adversary + non-mechanical workers stay on the strong models. Absent = every sub-task uses `worker`.

max_output_tokens.description: beta.99: output-token ceiling exported to the SDK subprocess as CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. Nothing previously set one, so every structured call inherited whatever ceiling the bundled SDK picked for the model id -- which is undefined for a model newer than the pinned SDK (e.g. claude-opus-5 against SDK 0.3.207). 0 disables (inherit the SDK default).

price_overrides.description: Per-model price overrides for cost estimation, keyed by model id. Values are USD per million tokens.

auth.description: Anthropic auth for the embedded Claude Agent SDK. Vault-first (credential_service), env fallback (api_key_env, default ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).

lead_timeout_seconds.description: beta.43: max seconds the lead-planner SDK call may run before it is treated as a hang and the run fails cleanly (loop.lead_timeout). The lead await was unbounded (beta.42 only bounded the worker); a healthy long plan was indistinguishable from a wedge.

stuck_loop_seconds.description: beta.40: reclaim threshold for a wedged loop. If run() is asked to start a session still marked running by the module-level re-entrancy guard, but its last_checkpoint_at/updated_at has not advanced for this many seconds, the tracked loop is treated as dead (torn down with a prior runtime on plugin re-register), the stale guard entry is force-cleared, and the fresh run proceeds. Must exceed a normal long worker SDK call so a busy loop is never reclaimed.

teardown_drain_seconds.description: beta.41: max seconds teardown() waits for a still-running loop from the runtime being torn down to finish before closing its state DB. A plugin re-register (OKF / gateway auto-discovery churn when plugins.allow is empty) schedules a fire-and-forget teardown of the previous runtime; closing the DB out from under an in-flight loop.run() crashes the run. Draining first prevents that. Bounded so a wedged loop can't block teardown forever.

stall_watchdog_seconds.description: beta.42: active stall-watchdog delay. When the re-entrancy guard skips a re-entry (loop.run_skipped_already_running) it arms a timer for this long, then re-checks the session's progress; if none, the wedged loop's stale guard handle is force-deregistered (loop.wedge_detected) so recovery/next-run can reclaim it. Makes beta.40's passive reclaim active -- a loop that wedges with no further re-register is now noticed.

subtask_deadline_seconds.description: beta.60: max wall-clock seconds a single sub-task's dispatch (runOne) may run before it is force-failed. beta.42 bounded only the worker SDK call, but runOne also awaits unbounded git/IO (worktreeHeadSha, readReactions, verify probes, recordSpend) between the row-flip-to-running and the worker spawn; a hang in any of those wedged the whole dispatcher (b59 PR#858 seq-7: 5h30m silent, row stuck running with sdk_session_id=null and no worker process). This bounds the entire runOne invocation. Must be >= worker_timeout_seconds plus IO margin.

budget_reserve_ratio.description: beta.61: fraction of the total session budget held in reserve for the pending adversary review + push while a cycle's review hasn't run yet. The pre-sub-task projection adds this reserve so the loop aborts early (before a sub-task that would leave no room to finish the cycle) instead of completing all sub-tasks and dying one review short of a PR (the b60 smoke failure). Clamped [0,0.9].

env_wait_retry_enabled.description: beta.53 (P1b): when a worker ends its turn awaiting a non-existent mid-turn 'Monitor event' (env-wait hallucination) and made no committed change, re-invoke the sub-task ONCE with corrective context (branched on whether it wrote-but-didn't-commit) instead of failing the run. Set false to disable the retry; the failure is still tagged loop.worker_env_wait_hallucination.

clarification_escalation_enabled.description: beta.55 (B2): when a worker refuses/confabulates a sub-task even after the beta.54 async-coord retry, pause the session in 'awaiting_clarification' (persisting the worker's question + paused seq, preserving the worktree) and surface it via harness_progress for a human to answer with harness_answer, instead of hard-failing the run. Set false to keep the terminal-fail behaviour.

graceful_pr_on_review_crash.description: beta.62 (fix #2/#3): when a cycle-N adversary review CRASHES (SDK/parse/persist error) instead of returning a verdict, and a PRIOR cycle already produced a completed review AND this cycle's own sub-task self-verification was fully green, open the PR anyway with merge_recommendation='needs_human_review' rather than discarding the adversary-motivated commits (the b60-attempt-2 silent-review-crash failure: 8 good commits, seq-6 self-verify green, cycle-2 review crashed, work thrown away). When the graceful path is NOT taken, the worktree is preserved (not released) so the commit chain stays inspectable. Set false to keep the hard-fail-and-release behaviour.

session_stall_seconds.description: beta.63 (Part A): session-level stall watchdog window. A session writes session.last_progress_at on EVERY state transition; the watchdog checks non-terminal executing/reviewing/finalising sessions where now-last_progress_at exceeds this and emits a loud loop.session_stalled, attempts bounded self-recovery (re-tick the loop-runner), and if unrecoverable transitions to a terminal failed(reason=stalled_no_progress) PRESERVING the worktree and, if the branch has commits, opening a graceful push+PR flagged needs_human_review. Must exceed the longest legit phase (adversary review + push); clamped to >=300.

stall_auto_terminal.description: beta.63 (Part A): sub-flag gating the AUTO-TERMINAL transition of a stalled session. When false, the watchdog still DETECTS + LOGS + attempts recovery, but never forces the terminal failed transition (detection/observability on, auto-transition off, kept separately toggleable per Carel).

stall_graceful_pr.description: beta.63 (Part A): on an UNRECOVERABLE stall with commits on the branch, attempt a graceful push + PR flagged needs_human_review (beta.62 pattern) so a near-done deliverable is not evaporated. Set false to fail-and-preserve-worktree only.

stall_sweep_interval_seconds.description: beta.67 (Bug A): EXTERNAL stall-sweep cadence (seconds). beta.63's checkStalls runs IN-PROCESS, so a dead loop-runner process cannot watchdog its own death (beta.66 smoke #4). This is the tick interval for the EXTERNAL stall-sweep service (registered like pr-watcher / retention-nightly) that runs loop.sweepStalls() independent of any loop process: it runs the existing checkStalls fast path AND reaps sessions with a pending cancel flag whose loop is dead (terminal failed reason=cancelled_dead_loop, worktree preserved). Default 60; clamped [15,600].

enforce_worker_context.description: beta.67 (P0a): enforce SUBSTANTIVE workerContext (rationale + file-anchored changeSpec/excerpt) on mutate/mixed sub-tasks at validatePlan. true (default) -> one bounded lead re-ask then hard-throw; false -> WARN-only escape hatch. Enforces the founding orchestrator-split goal (cheap workers implement from Fable's investigation instead of re-scanning).

revise_spec_turn_enabled.description: beta.67 (P0b): run ONE Fable revise-spec turn between the adversary and cycle-2 workers to refresh workerContext with a resolved changeSpec, so workers never see the raw adversary findings (the beta.63/64 no-op regression). false -> beta.66 raw-findings behaviour; a revise-spec failure also falls back. Default true.

revise_spec_timeout_seconds.description: beta.84 (#2): hard timeout (seconds) on the Fable revise-spec turn. The turn is an unbounded lead-model call that has spun ~570s then failed on the ambient cron lane cap (beta.73 signature, session 1c744d70) -- ~10 min burned before falling back to raw findings. Bounding it makes the raw-findings fallback FAST (audited loop.revise_spec_timeout) instead of eating the lane cap. 0 disables the bound. Default 180.

skip_observe_reprobe_on_revise.description: beta.70 (F5): skip an observe-only sub-task's re-probe on a revise cycle when the same seq already completed cleanly in a prior cycle (PR #870 re-ran the seq-1 probe for 58s/$0.29 despite the revise-spec saying 'no changes'). Default true.

revise_scoping_enabled.description: beta.91 (Fix 1): on a revise cycle, skip sub-tasks whose file scope does not intersect any review finding's file (already-correct from a prior cycle; the DR/BCP smoke re-ran 8 of 12 no-change sub-tasks). A finding with no resolvable file makes the cycle unscopable => run every sub-task (conservative). Never skips a sub-task a kept one depends on. Default true; false restores beta.90 run-all.

parallel_independent_subtasks.description: beta.117: run independent sub-tasks (disjoint declared file scope, no dependency) concurrently, up to subtask_concurrency. Each concurrent worker gets its OWN checkout on its own branch, and its commits are merged back into the session branch one at a time; two workers touching the same undeclared file surface as a merge conflict against a named sub-task instead of silently corrupting each other. Costs one `npm ci` per slot, once per cycle. Default false. Set true AND subtask_concurrency > 1 to parallelise.

deterministic_revise_mapping.description: beta.92: use the DETERMINISTIC finding->sub-task mapping on a revise cycle instead of the deleted LLM revise-spec turn (which kept timing out on the cron lane cap across b89/b90/b91 and falling back to a raw finding-dump that induced worker confabs). Maps each diff-addressable finding (spec|quality|security, .file required) to the sub-task(s) owning its file via strict resolveContractPath; broadcasts meta (fit|runtime) findings + mapping-misses to all sub-tasks (never dropped). Default true; false restores the beta.56 whole-review raw hint fallback.

worker_confab_detect.description: beta.92 (log-only): emit loop.worker_confab_suspected when the worker's final message lexically claims it left a contract-REQUIRED (non-relaxed) file untouched (the b91 seq-6 confab). No behaviour change -- verification still decides pass/fail. Default true; false disables the detector.

contract_rederive_enabled.description: beta.76 + beta.93 kill-switch: correct a stale lead-guessed contract path against the repo's real touched layout BEFORE verification (with the beta.93 exact-match short-circuit + same-basename evidence guards, so a correctly-committed path is never rewritten -- the session de0cba9f false-positive). Default true; false disables re-derivation entirely (verify against the declared path verbatim, relying on the beta.50+ tolerant match rules).

contract_test_path_reconcile.description: beta.100: bounded TEST-CONTRACT reconciliation. Rewrite a contract path that is a TEST file and does not structurally resolve against what the sub-task actually touched onto that sub-task's own committed test file -- ONLY when exactly one such unmatched test contract and exactly one unclaimed committed test file exist, so the pairing is unambiguous. Closes the b99 seq-3 failure (session 4420aa45), where the lead guessed a co-located route.test.ts and the worker correctly used the repo's real Jest __tests__/ location; the beta.76 prefix-remapper could not help because the two paths share no trailing directory chain. Cannot re-open the beta.84 sibling false-positive: a non-test contract path never enters the rule. Default true; false restores the pre-b100 strict failure.

contract_mismatch_escalation_enabled.description: beta.100: when a sub-task made a REAL commit but its files do not match the contract paths, pause in awaiting_clarification (worktree + commits preserved, resumable via harness_answer) instead of hard-failing the run. The sub-task still FAILS verification and nothing is accepted -- only the terminal disposition changes. Closes the b99 seq-3 death, where the b53 env-wait retry (needs no commit), the b35 revise no-op (needs cycle > 1) and the b55 refusal escalation (needs no commit) all missed a worker that had committed correct work. Default true; false restores the pre-b100 hard fail.

ledger_reachability_guard_enabled.description: beta.101: before the adversary SDK call, cross-check every commit_sha in the sub-task ledger for reachability from HEAD, and fail the run with an explicit ledger_commits_unreachable reason when any is missing. Detects a branch that has silently lost work the run already committed. In the b100 smoke (session 3c6c1608) a clarification resume reset the branch to origin/main and orphaned six recorded commits; nothing noticed until the adversary blocked on the absence of work that had in fact been written correctly, after a paid review turn. The b101 preserve-local-branch fix removes that specific trigger; this guard is the independent detector for the next one. Fails OPEN -- a git probe error never blocks a healthy run. Default true.

plan_path_validation_enabled.description: beta.101: at plan time, flag any filesLikelyTouched entry that names a file whose PARENT DIRECTORY does not exist in the repo, and fold a warning into that sub-task's worker dispatch telling it to treat the path as a guess and locate the real convention. The parent directory is the discriminator: planning a file that does not exist yet is normal (most sub-tasks create files), but a file in a directory that does not exist either is usually invented. In the b100 smoke the lead planned src/components/layout/grc-nav.tsx when src/components/layout/ does not exist, costing a failed verify, a clarification round-trip, a re-plan and a review turn. Advisory only -- new modules legitimately create new directories, so this never blocks. Default true.

plan_path_writeback_enabled.description: beta.103: once verification proves a contract path correction (the b76 rederive or the b100 test reconcile), write that correction back into the sub-task's filesLikelyTouched so the rest of the run reasons about the real path. Before b103 a correction only ever reached the local contract array, so the plan kept the lead's fictional path -- and both computeReviseScope and mapFindingsToSubTasks key off filesLikelyTouched. In the b102 smoke (PR #906) the lead planned src/app/(app)/... where the repo uses (portal); verification rederived it and the sub-task passed, but on cycle 3 the scoper could not intersect the adversary's (portal) findings with the plan's (app) path, skipped that sub-task, and shipped a PR blocked on a one-character lint error it had been told about for three cycles. Only ever REWRITES a path the plan already declared, never appends, so a sub-task's scope can be corrected but never widened. Default true.

lead_repo_scout_enabled.description: beta.104: give the lead a READ-ONLY look at the repository before it plans. Until b104 every lead call ran through structuredCall with tools:[] and Read/Glob/Grep explicitly disallowed, and the worktree did not exist yet (runLeadPlanner calls the lead model first and allocateWorktree afterwards) -- so the lead planned entire features, file paths and code excerpts included, having never opened a single file of the repo. The b67 gate simultaneously REQUIRED every mutate sub-task to carry workerContext.codeExcerpts described as 'the ACTUAL code you read, verbatim', which the lead could not have read, so the harness was mandating plausible fabrication and then spending the rest of the run detecting it: the b63 conventions ingest, the b76 rederive, the b100 test reconcile, the b101 suspect-path check and the b103 writeback are all downstream of this one blindfold. In the b102 smoke loop.plan_paths_suspect counted seven fictional paths in a single plan ((app) where the repo uses (portal), components/layout where it uses components/ui), and the workers re-explored the repo anyway -- context that is confidently wrong is worse than none. With this enabled the lead first runs a scout turn in a real worktree with Read/Glob/Grep and no write tools, then the existing toolless planning call receives that report as its only admissible source of repo facts. The planning call itself is unchanged, which preserves the b28/b40 protection against a tool-enabled planner wandering off and writing its plan to a file. The adversary never sees the report -- its prompt is built from a hand-written projection of the brief, not the brief object -- so reviewer independence is unaffected. Best-effort: unwired, disabled, no resolvable repoHint, a throw or an empty report all fall back to the pre-b104 blind plan. Default true.

lead_scout_timeout_seconds.description: beta.106: wall-clock ceiling on the lead's repo scout turn, now ADDED to lead_timeout_seconds by the loop instead of being carved out of it. b104 nested the scout inside the lead budget without raising it: with the shipped defaults (lead 900s, scout 600s) that left 300s for planning, and planning alone measured 441s and 182s on b103 -- arithmetic that never closed, and the b105 smoke duly died at exactly 900s after the scout started with the lead mid-plan. Note this is the SOFT bound: aborting the wall clock signals the SDK but cannot interrupt a tool call already in flight, so the harness stops WAITING 30s past this ceiling and plans with the partial report, letting the SDK unwind in the background. lead_scout_max_turns is the hard bound. Exceeding either costs the scout only -- the run continues, with a partial report or blind.

lead_scout_max_turns.description: beta.106: hard ceiling on scout agent turns. The b105 smoke (session b08502aa) scouted for FOURTEEN MINUTES against a 600s budget: aborting the wall clock signals the SDK but cannot interrupt a tool call already in flight, so the abort fired at 600s and the scout still ran to roughly 850s. The SDK turn cap is the only bound that reliably holds. 60 turns is enough to find one analogue, read it, verify the paths the plan will name and note the traps, and deliberately not enough to survey a codebase; the scout prompt states the same budget in words so the model spends it deliberately rather than being truncated mid-exploration.

lead_scout_max_chars.description: beta.107: ceiling on the scout report folded into the lead planning prompt. Raised 20000 -> 32000: b106 reported reportChars 20049, the exact length produced by truncating at 20000, so the ceiling was binding on an ordinary brief with nothing in the trail saying so. Truncation is now MIDDLE-OUT, keeping both ends -- the head carries locations and conventions, the tail carries the traps, and head-only truncation was dropping precisely the repo rules the plan needed. b98 is why a ceiling exists at all: an oversized lead input cost a whole run when the reply breached the output ceiling.

resume_ledger_guard_enabled.description: beta.105: also run the ledger reachability guard at RESUME, immediately after a re-plan re-allocates the worktree, not only before adversary review. b101 built the guard and wired it in one place. The b103 smoke (session b8ece861) then lost eight of ten recorded commits when a clarification resume re-allocated onto a different tip, stalled at a second clarification and was aborted -- so the guard never ran at all and the loss surfaced four hours later in a hand-written post-mortem. Re-allocation is the operation that loses commits, so it is where the check belongs. A fresh run has an empty ledger and short-circuits, so this costs one no-op call on the common path.

basename_rescue_enabled.description: beta.105: generate a path remap from the mismatch itself instead of escalating to a human. b103's rederive only corrects a contract path when an EARLIER sub-task already taught the run the substitution; it has no producer. On the b103 smoke, seq 9 was the first sub-task to touch src/components/, so the lead's fictional components/layout/sidebar.tsx met the worker's correct components/ui/sidebar.tsx with no lesson to apply, no rederive fired, and a mechanically-obvious correction cost an hour of clarification dead time. Fires only when the mismatch is a SINGLE file, the basenames match, the planned directory is absent from the repo and the committed directory is present -- and even then only continues if re-verification against the corrected contract actually passes.

file_written_accepts_rename.description: beta.105: accept a file_written contract when git shows the path was ADDED or RENAMED-TO inside the sub-task's own commit range, even though the blob's mtime predates the sub-task. mtime is a proxy for authorship and git mv preserves it, so a worker that correctly moves a file onto the contract's path produced a file_committed PASS and a file_written FAIL on the same file in the same commit (b103 smoke seq 3). Two checks disagreeing about one file is incoherent verifier state, not a safety property. Presence and non-emptiness on disk are still required, and the range is the sub-task's own, so a merely pre-existing file still fails.

sdk_first_token_timeout_seconds.description: beta.64 (P0-1) / beta.65 (P0): PHASE-2 first-token watchdog window (seconds). Armed inside consumeWorkerStream when the SDK stream OPENS (system/init) and disarmed on the first assistant content block (text/tool_use). No first content block within this window => abort with the distinct stopReason first_token_timeout so the loop retries on a fresh session. beta.65 split-phase redesign: phase 2 (stream-open -> first-token) is always near-instant on success (4-5ms in smoke #3), so the default is LOWERED 90 -> 30. The pre-stream stall is covered by sdk_stream_open_timeout_seconds (phase 1). Clamped [10,1800].

sdk_stream_open_timeout_seconds.description: beta.65 (P0): PHASE-1 stream-open watchdog window (seconds). A SEPARATE timer armed at CALL INITIATION (top of consumeWorkerStream, BEFORE the stream opens) and disarmed when the stream opens (system/init). If the stream never opens within this window, the call is aborted with the same distinct stopReason first_token_timeout so the loop retries on a FRESH SDK session. Covers the beta.64 gap: a PRE-STREAM POST hang (SDK streaming POST never returns its first byte -- smoke #3: 28+min silence, no sdk_stream_opened, no abort) that beta.64's stream-open-armed watchdog never saw. Phase 1 is highly variable even on success (smoke #3: 47s / 422s-succeeded / >1800s-hung), so a legit-but-slow open like 422s WILL be aborted -- CORRECT, because the abort routes into the same first_token_timeout -> one-fresh-session retry path (a cold/unpooled open is fast on retry). Clamped [10,600].

worker_stream_idle_warn_seconds.description: beta.90 (Feature 2): worker STREAM-SLOW idle-warn window (seconds). Inside consumeWorkerStream, once the worker SDK stream has OPENED, a 30s tick watches for token/message activity; if the stream goes IDLE (no delta) for this many seconds it emits loop.worker_stream_slow and bumps the session liveness heartbeat (last_progress_at) so harness_progress surfaces 'worker stream idle Ns' instead of the phase looking wedged. OBSERVABILITY ONLY -- it NEVER aborts (a slow stream recovered on b89; a blunt abort would have wrongly killed it). Root cause: session 041bd3d3 sub-task 2, worker stream opened then went idle ~15 min with no signal in harness_progress. Default 90; clamped [30,600].

worker_timeout_retry_enabled.description: beta.64 (P0-2): when a worker sub-task fails with a first_token_timeout OR a worker timeout, RETRY it ONCE on a FRESH SDK session (no resumeSessionId) before flipping the run terminal. The retry re-verifies; a pass completes the sub-task, a fail falls through to the existing terminal path using the retry's result. Max 1 retry per sub-task.

best_effort_verify.description: beta.64 (P0-3): BEST-EFFORT VERIFY. If a VERIFY sub-task (observe-mode, the last/verify sub-task) times out even after the P0-2 retry, AND the prior mutate sub-task's verify_probe was GREEN, AND git diff-stat shows only expected files touched, mark the run verify_skipped (reason worker_timeout), push the branch, and open the PR flagged merge_recommendation=needs_human_review (reusing the beta.62 graceful-PR machinery) rather than discarding shippable work. This is what SHOULD have happened in beta.63 smoke #2 -- the code was shippable, only the verifier hung.

scripted_verify_fallback.description: beta.64 (P0-4): SCRIPTED VERIFIER FALLBACK. When an observe-mode VERIFY sub-task times out, run a DETERMINISTIC fallback -- npx tsc --noEmit + git diff --stat + the allowlisted repo check scripts -- LOCALLY in the worktree. beta.85: DEFAULT FALSE. This was the last remaining local-execution path, against the hard 'never run the repo suite locally, ever' rule (verification is CI-only since beta.81). Opt in explicitly if you want the local deterministic rescue; the default no longer runs anything locally.

recovery_max_resumes.description: beta.81 (Track C / C4): recovery-resume circuit breaker. When MORE than this many recovery.auto_resuming events fire for the SAME session within recovery_resume_window_seconds, the harness HARD-STOPS that session (marks it failed, reason recovery_bounce_loop) and surfaces it to a human instead of resuming again (forensic d01a7484 bounce loop).

recovery_resume_window_seconds.description: beta.81 (Track C / C4): window (seconds) over which recovery_max_resumes auto-resumes for a single session trip the circuit breaker.

recovery_resume_at_subtask.description: beta.81 (Track C / C3): when a session left mid-executing is recovered, RESUME AT the failed/incomplete sub-task (mark the orphaned running sub-task failed, preserve completed sub-task commits) instead of re-planning the whole session from scratch (which re-burns completed sub-tasks). Set false to restore the pre-beta.81 full-restart recovery behaviour.

lead_json_retry_enabled.description: beta.81 (Track C): give the LEAD re-plan SDK call the same retry-once-on-extractJson-failure guard the classifier has, so a transient prose-drift (lead returns prose instead of the JSON plan contract) does not hard-crash the plan.

require_worker_context_strict.description: beta.99: what to do when a plan still lacks substantive workerContext after the bounded re-ask. false (default) ships the degraded plan with a loud warning -- workers on those seqs simply start colder. true restores the pre-beta.99 hard-fail. The default flipped because b98 (session f2613eec) burned an entire session and produced nothing while the harness was holding a valid plan.

lead_salvage_truncated_plan.description: beta.99: when BOTH lead plan attempts are cut off at the output ceiling, salvage the well-formed prefix of the reply instead of failing the run with plan_failed. The salvaged plan is REAL but INCOMPLETE (trailing sub-tasks were cut off) and is logged loudly as such; it still has to pass validatePlan. Set false to restore the pre-beta.99 hard-fail.

deterministic_final_scope_check.description: beta.94 (Feature 1): DETERMINISTIC FINAL SCOPE CHECK. (a) Elide a trailing PURE-OBSERVE scope/boundary 'final verification' sub-task from the worker plan (taskMode observe, no mutate verify, description matches scope|boundar|final-verif|nothing-outside) -- it has nothing to write so a worker can go idle on it indefinitely (the b93 seq-12 stall) while adding zero signal. Audited as loop.final_verify_subtask_elided. (b) After the last mutate sub-task, compare the files committed in <base>..HEAD against the UNION of every sub-task's declared file scope; a committed file outside the union folds into the adversary review as a fit/medium ReviewFinding (never a hard fail). Audited as loop.final_scope_check_ran / loop.final_scope_check_out_of_scope. Default true.

worker_idle_abort_enabled.description: beta.94 (Feature 2): NARROW IDLE-NO-WORK ABORT. loop.worker_idle_no_work fires (LOG-ONLY) when the conjunction holds: >= worker_idle_consecutive_slow consecutive worker_stream_slow ticks, all with tokensOut===0, cumulative elapsed > worker_idle_min_elapsed_seconds, AND no worktree writes during the sub-task (the b93 seq-12 signature). When this flag is TRUE the same conjunction ALSO aborts the sub-task cleanly via the existing WorkerTimeoutError / {outcome:'timeout'} terminal path (worktree preserved -- no new terminal path). Default FALSE (beta.90 observability-only behaviour preserved).

worker_idle_consecutive_slow.description: beta.94 (Feature 2): number of CONSECUTIVE loop.worker_stream_slow ticks (all with tokensOut===0) required before loop.worker_idle_no_work may fire. Default 3; clamped [2,20].

worker_idle_min_elapsed_seconds.description: beta.94 (Feature 2): minimum cumulative elapsed (seconds) inside the worker stream before loop.worker_idle_no_work may fire. Default 900 (15 min); clamped [60,3600].

revise_max_adoptions_per_cycle.description: beta.108: ceiling on orphan-finding adoptions per revise cycle. Adoption widens a sub-task's file scope, and scope is what a revise cycle costs. The b106 revise on PR #932 fired 21 mapping misses across two cycles against the original smoke's two, because the adversary re-reads the whole branch each cycle and keeps surfacing adjacent issues; uncapped adoption would pull most of the branch back into every cycle. Candidates are taken in severity order, and info-severity findings are never adopted -- info is how the adversary records that a PRIOR finding was verified fixed.

revise_route_co_fix_owners.description: beta.119: also route a finding to the owners of the OTHER files its fix needs (the adversary's `relatedFiles`, plus any repo path the finding's prose names). The b118 smoke raised 'the upload route discards the kind/title fields the drawer sends' in all three cycles and fixed it in none: routing was correct, but the route file's owner could not act alone -- persisting the fields needed a Prisma column it did not own, and removing the dead dropdown needed the drawer it did not own. It reported no-change, indistinguishable from 'already correct', and the finding was re-raised until the cycle ceiling. Set false for pre-b119 single-owner routing.

max_cycle_extensions.description: beta.119: extra execute+review cycles the loop may grant itself past max_cycles when the adversary's finding count is trending DOWN and this run's own average cycle cost still fits inside the session ceiling and the per-user daily cap. b97 already detected this arc and merely asked the operator to re-run harness_revise by hand; the b118 smoke went 16 -> 8 -> 9 findings and stopped on the ceiling having spent $12.90 of $30, shipping four blocking findings its own report called small and mechanical. Both conditions must hold, so a stuck run (flat or rising findings) still stops on time. Set 0 to restore the pre-b119 hard ceiling.

workflow_scope_precheck.description: beta.119: when the plan intends to edit .github/workflows/**, verify the routed token carries the `workflow` scope BEFORE running any sub-task. The CI-optimisation run planned a one-line ci.yml change, executed it, reviewed it, and learned only at the push that GitHub refuses workflow writes without that scope -- answerable from the plan and a response header before the first worker started. Only a token that PROVABLY lacks the scope stops a run; fine-grained PATs and GitHub App tokens report no scope header and are waved through, since 'cannot tell' must not read as 'cannot do'.

scope_blowout_file_threshold.description: beta.110: out-of-scope committed file count at which a cycle is abandoned BEFORE adversary review, instead of folding the overage into the review as a `fit` finding. On ProjectThanos PR #932 an in-worktree npm cache was swept into a commit by git add -A; the check reported 12423 out-of-scope files, produced a finding, and let the run continue -- the adversary then hit its 900s timeout on a 12432-file diff and the session died having pushed nothing, stranding eight good commits. A diff that size cannot be reviewed, so discovering that slowly is pure loss. Set 0 to disable and keep the pre-b110 finding-only behaviour.

ship_when_no_blocking_findings.description: beta.109: end the review loop when the adversary says `revise` but no finding is diff-addressable at medium severity or above. The adversary writes `revise` while ANY finding is open, including the informational ones it emits to record that a prior finding was fixed, so a run converges to a floor it can never cross: ProjectThanos PR #932 went 18 -> 15 -> 17 across three cycles and finished with ten low, six info and one low convention finding, nothing at medium or above, over three separate revises. Medium and above still cycles, so this cannot ship real defects; the residual lows go on the PR body and harness_revise picks them up on request.

auto_resolve_satisfied_contract.description: beta.111: settle a contract mismatch from the branch's own history instead of pausing the run for a human, when every expected path the sub-task did not touch was already changed by an earlier commit on this branch. Findings are often written conditionally ("if the handler extends `to` unconditionally..."); a worker that reads the code, finds the condition already handled and commits only a test then trips the contract check. That escalated on two runs running -- b109 sub-task 2 and b110 sub-task 5, the latter idle for forty minutes at $2.99 waiting for someone to type "skip" -- on evidence the harness already held in git. Strict: one expected path never touched on this branch and it still asks.

early_exit_no_change_cycle.description: beta.108: end a revise cycle that moved the branch tip nowhere instead of buying an adversary pass over an unchanged diff. The b106 revise's cycle 3 dispatched five sub-tasks, four returned subtask_revise_no_change, and the run still paid for a full review. Applies from cycle 2 only, and only when a prior review exists to carry forward.

revise_adopt_orphan_findings.description: beta.107: when an adversary finding names a file that no sub-task's plan claims, let the nearest sub-task adopt it so a worker is actually asked to fix it. b92 broadcasts such a finding to every sub-task as context, which never drops it but never targets it either, and b91 scoping then skips those sub-tasks because their files intersect no finding. On b106 the help-content.ts convention finding was raised in both revise cycles, owned by nobody, and could not have been closed however many cycles the run was given. Adoption prefers a sub-task the finding's own prose names, else the nearest in the directory tree, and leaves a finding that matches neither as a pure broadcast.

worker_timeout_max_attempts.description: beta.113: total worker attempts for a timeout-class failure, including the first. Two attempts was one retry, against the same too-short first-token window.

worker_first_token_retry_multiplier.description: beta.113: widen the first-token watchdog on each retry, so a slow start gets a wider window instead of the identical one that just failed (30s -> 90s -> 270s). 1 disables escalation.

worker_first_token_retry_cap_seconds.description: beta.113: ceiling for the escalated first-token window.

ci.description: beta.81 (Track B): CI-verification shift. After a branch is pushed, the harness polls the commit's combined GitHub status/check-runs and treats CI as the verification spine.

wait_timeout_seconds.description: beta.81 (B2): max wall-clock seconds the harness waits for CI to finish after pushing a branch before it treats the wait as a SOFT checkpoint (surfaces 'CI still running after N min on <sha>' and offers a resumable continue-watching -- never a hard fail). Clamped [30, 7200].

poll_interval_seconds.description: beta.81 (B2): poll interval (seconds) for the post-push CI wait; the harness re-queries getCombinedStatus(headSha) every this-many seconds until it is not pending or the wait_timeout_seconds elapses. Clamped [5, 300].

none_grace_seconds.description: beta.91 (F4): grace window (seconds) for an authored-this-cycle CI workflow to REGISTER on GitHub before the harness concludes 'no CI'. Fixes the b90 bug where the harness shipped a merge recommendation 0.5s after push, before its own workflow registered, then CI later caught a real typecheck error. Only applies when a workflow was authored this cycle; a genuine no-CI repo still returns none fast. A still-none result after the grace window is a distinct NON-blocking authored_workflow_never_registered outcome (merge still recommended, but the human sees CI did not verify the SHA). 0 disables (beta.90 terminate-on-first-none). Clamped [0, 300].

api_key_env.description: Env-var fallback for the Vercel token when the vault is unavailable or empty.

deploy_repair.description: beta.36: post-merge deploy-repair loop. On a merged PR whose Vercel deploy ERRORs, auto-attempt fixes (up to max_attempts new PRs) from the build logs; if still failing, revert all merges and leave the last attempt open for review.

budget_ratio.description: Repair budget as a fraction of budgets.daily_max_usd, shared across all attempts.

pat_routing.description: Git credential routing. beta.25 hierarchical shape (github/gitlab -> org -> person -> {token,name,email,slack_user_id}) plus legacy flat fields. See docs/GITHUB_AUTH.md.

github.description: Hierarchical GitHub routing: org -> person -> {token:{value|env|vault}, name, email, slack_user_id}.

gitlab.description: Hierarchical GitLab routing: org -> person -> {token:{value|env|vault}, name, email, slack_user_id}.

commit_identity.description: Legacy per-user commit identity (superseded by hierarchical name/email).

logging.description: Harness log verbosity. 'debug' makes error sites log full error objects.

brief.description: beta.63 (convention-awareness Fix 1): brief construction / repo-convention ingest tuning.

ingest_repo_conventions.description: beta.63 (Fix 1): at brief build, ingest the checked-out repo's declared convention files (.cursor/rules/**, .cursorrules, CONTRIBUTING.md, CONVENTIONS.md, AGENTS.md, .github/CONTRIBUTING.md) into the optional brief field repoConventions[] so the lead + worker + adversary SDK prompts (which get NO OpenClaw context injection) explicitly carry them.

convention_char_budget.description: beta.63 (Fix 1): total char budget for the ingested conventions block. Over budget, the LONGEST sources are truncated first with a note, rather than dropping sources silently.

repo_only_invariant.description: beta.80 (F1): the crystalliser is told the harness is a REPO tool. External-API side-effect acceptance criteria are reframed into 'build the code + a test', never 'perform the live call'. Live API calls are legitimate only as test/verify steps against code just written. Set false to restore the pre-beta.80 crystalliser prompt.

bimodal_clarify.description: beta.80 (F2): the crystalliser self-reports competing readings of a brief; when >= bimodal_min_interpretations distinct readings (or an explicit clarificationNeeded) exist, the run PAUSES for a hard clarify (pause-and-wait, no session started) instead of guessing one reading. Set false to always proceed.

bimodal_min_interpretations.description: beta.80 (F2): how many distinct crystalliser interpretations force a clarify pause. Default 2.

run_repo_check_scripts.description: beta.81 (Track B / B4): the LOCAL check-script runner is RETIRED from the verification spine -- verification is CI-only now (Carel: 'I do not want it to run locally, ever'). Default false. When true (opt-in), the final-verify sub-task runs repo-declared check scripts inline in the worktree (beta.63 behaviour) as REVISE-worthy findings. The runner plumbing is otherwise kept only for the scripted-verify FALLBACK of a timed-out observe VERIFY sub-task, NOT as a verify gate.

check_script_allowlist.description: beta.63 (Fix 2): allowlist of package.json script names the harness may run in final-verify. A discovered script NOT on this list is NEVER run.

check_script_timeout_seconds.description: beta.63 (Fix 2): per-check-script wall-clock timeout (seconds). A timed-out script is treated as unrunnable (non-fatal log + note), not a hard fail.

typecheck_gate.description: beta.111: run the repo's own typecheck script before review and raise a `high` finding for errors in files this branch changed. The adversary reviews the diff, not the compiler: ProjectThanos PR #932 survived three revise runs with `TS2551: Property 'ownerUserId' does not exist`, introduced by the b108 revise, and that repo's CI does not run a typecheck so CI stayed green. Errors in untouched files are ignored, so a repo with pre-existing breakage (#932 also carries 71 unrelated failing tests) is still usable. One script per cycle, unlike run_repo_check_scripts which runs the whole suite and stays off by default.

check_script_heap_retry_mb.description: beta.70 (F4): V8 heap ceiling (MB) applied via NODE_OPTIONS on the retry after a check script dies of a heap OOM (exit 134 / 'Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit'). On Thanos-scale repos tsc --noEmit OOMs at the 4 GB default; 8 GB clears it. A persisted OOM after the retry becomes a BLOCKING finding. Default 8192.

log.description: beta.63 (Part B): durable, structured, append-only interaction log written OUTSIDE the git worktree (in the harness data dir). Captures every SDK/LLM call, state transition, verify probe, and stall/recovery event so a near-completion failure leaves a complete, greppable trail that survives a worktree release + container restart. Secret redaction on write is mandatory and NOT disableable.

interaction_log_enabled.description: beta.63 (Part B): master switch for the interaction log.

dir.description: beta.63 (Part B): directory for the JSONL logs. Default <dataDir>/logs where dataDir is the directory holding the state DB. Leave empty for the default.

full_prompts.description: beta.63 (Part B): when false (DEFAULT) only prompt SIZES + TAILS are logged, not full prompt bodies (transcripts can be huge + sensitive). Set true for deep-debug. This does NOT disable secret redaction — redaction on write is always applied.

retention_days.description: beta.63 (Part B): prune per-session log files older than this many days.
